correctness.rationale: For one new universal vertex \(c\), the neighborhood complex is exactly \(\Delta(V(H))\cup(c*\mathcal N(H))\) with intersection \(\mathcal N(H)\). The two pieces are contractible and the inclusions are simplicial cofibrations, so their homotopy pushout is \(\Sigma\mathcal N(H)\). Iterating gives the clique-join statement. For \(nK_m\), the base neighborhood complex is the disjoint union of \(n\) copies of \(S^{m-2}\), and the suspension decomposition yields the displayed wedge formula. The packaged checker verifies the exact one-step complex identity on three bases and the predicted mod-two homology on ten finite family members; these computations corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The result is an operation law for the Lovász neighborhood complex, not a parameter-specific census: joining any eligible graph with a complete graph becomes iterated suspension. This supplies immediate all-parameter homotopy types for natural block/windmill families and explains a systematic dimension shift under adjoining universal vertices. The exact two-sphere-dimension wedge formula for \(K_r\vee(nK_m)\) is a reusable structural consequence rather than a routine table lookup.
